system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  1 inherited memory before committing. Name it by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memory you want verified (up to one, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale:
Two of the three concurrent problems are funnel-mechanics problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue. That argues against promotional_pricing (memory_73): matching a competitor's entry price buys price-sensitive accounts that are structurally the least durable revenue, and it does nothing about the internal funnel decay. referral_incentive (memory_57) works on established customers and does not touch the leak. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is a different segment entirely from the SMB pressure. That leaves simplify_onboarding vs activation_messaging, and both memories supporting simplification (memory_31 on signup fields, memory_86 on onboarding length) point at the exact metric that is declining, with onboarding sitting upstream of activation, so a fix there plausibly recovers part of both drops.

I am spending the single verification on memory_86 because it is the load-bearing claim for the provisional direction and the one most likely to be fragile. memory_31 is about cutting signup fields, which is adjacent but not the same intervention as shortening onboarding; memory_86 is the direct precedent, it is 24 days old, and it reports completion-rate and time-to-value lifts without any statement about downstream qualified revenue. Shorter onboarding can lift completion while admitting less-qualified accounts, which would be a false positive against my actual objective. If the archived record shows the lift was clean and revenue-bearing, I confirm simplify_onboarding. If it shows the effect was completion-only, confounded, or driven by a segment that does not match today's traffic, I switch to activation_messaging (memory_91), which addresses the larger 6% drop directly and is the natural fallback.
